stem.en: Can simply making a successful cell larger keep making it better?

text.en: Yes, a larger cell is always more powerful and efficient.

feedback.en: Larger cells have advantages, but they also face increasing transport and coordination problems. Bigger is not always better.

text.en: Yes, because larger cells can store more amounts of instructions (DNA)

feedback.en: Larger cells can store more DNA, but not an unlimited amount. More importantly, simply adding DNA does not solve the problems caused by increased cell size.

text.en: No, as a cell grows, its volume increases much faster than its surface area, making material exchange inefficient.

explanation.en: As a cell grows, its volume increases faster than its surface area. Eventually there isn't enough membrane area to exchange materials quickly enough to support the larger volume.
